documented_probe: : systematic test-case generation via the Category-Partition Method over a TSL-like specification. The agent must implement the documented frame-generation algorithm (base choices per strategy, [default]/[single]/[error] property rules, constraint repair by minimal deviation with lexicographic tie-break, canonical frame order, frame_limit truncation, and the documented unsatisfiable-with-reason result) as a CLI, and produce the visible frames.json. The verifier recomputes frames with an independent implementation for the visible spec and three hidden TSL specs (conflicting constraints, all-single parameters, an unsatisfiable combination) under several hidden params.json files (both strategies plus a frame-limit cap), compares exact JSON, re-checks byte determinism across repeated runs, and probes the documented exit codes on malformed specs/params.
notes: Medium: the core is a single self-contained Python deliverable implementing a multi-part deterministic algorithm (parse TSL with properties/values/ranges; strategy-dependent base and default-fill computation; constraint satisfaction via documented minimal-deviation repair; canonical grouping base/single/ordinary/error; unsatisfiable handling; id renumbering under frame_limit). reasoning_depth and debugging_ambiguity are moderate because the exact semantics (fill vs base, exclusion of non-base singles from repair, lexicographic tie-break) are documented but require careful reading and cross-checking against the visible fixture; adversarial_inputs covers malformed specs/params exit codes plus degenerate all-single and unsatisfiable specs; hidden_case_generalization is high because the deliverable must generalize to unseen TSL specs and params variants (hardcoding the visible 9-frame output fails every hidden case); quantitative_correctness enforced by exact JSON equality against an independent recompute and byte determinism between runs.
